main_text.l: Forte inter viduas (miserum!) cultoris arenas,
Et tesqua, & dumos, necnon & inhospita saxa,
Iacobi proles, ignara viaque, locorumque
Errabat, varia greffus ambage retexens.
Sæua plaga facies, atque infcia vomeris, æstu
Torrida, non illic clamor, strepitúsve rotarum,
Altáve tornata rupere silentia buxus.
Vilia non illic figit mapalia pastor,
Cæspitibúsve nouis congesta cacumina fúmant,
Nulla hominum apparent vestigia, vastus vbique
Campus, & obscura cælum se fornice pandit,
Et confecta situ regio, & nigrantia lustra
Dirarum latebris domus opportuna ferarum.
Hic, inter nemora, & lucos, Hebræa propago
Sola vagabatur, sancto de sanguine Creti
Isaída, Domino charissima pignora nuper,
Tunc inopes rerum, & lympha, victúque carentes
Audiit Omnipotens, & opis miseratus egenos,
Per desertá viæ regem se præbuit, vtque
Certum illis constaret iter, mirabile dictu,
Erexit gemina ætherias vexilla sub auras,
Luce refulgebát nubes, noctu aureus ignis
Vincebat piceas claro splendore tenebras.
Isacidum auspiciis Domini stetit agmen, eisdem
Et conclamauit vasa, & properante refixit
Signa manu, campoque acies immisit apertos
Nulla die, noctisque illi discrimina curæ,
Nóxque diésque Deus, simul ac is iusserat, ibat, Aut

page.notes: Printed text is a Latin poem in long lines, set as verse with each line as its own line; the text above is run as continuous paragraphs of verse lines, with line breaks preserved as printed where the source is verse. The final word "Aut" is a catchword-like fragment at the right, below the last line; it is kept in the text as printed. Possible doubtful readings: "Cæspitibúsve", "tornata", "Hebræa", "Isaída", "Isacidum", "vasa", "noctu" and "Vilia" should be checked against the scan at high magnification. The long-s forms have been normalised to plain s; the italic stanza lines are not marked with <i> here and should be restored.
